Paragraph:
Translation: As the embodied soul continually passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. The self-realized soul is not bewildered by such a change.

Purport (Excerpt): Since every living entity is an individual soul, each is changing his body every moment, manifesting sometimes as a child, sometimes as a youth, and sometimes as an old man. Yet the same spirit soul is there and does not undergo any change. This individual soul finally changes the body at death and transmigrates to another body...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna needs to understand how the eternal soul relates to the dying body to fully grasp why he shouldn't grieve.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna uses a simple, observable analogy: just as we naturally accept the transition of our body from childhood to adulthood to old age without losing our sense of 'self,' death is merely the final transition to a new body.
Outcome/Resolution: Death is reframed from a catastrophic end to a natural, inevitable biological transition (reincarnation).

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.reframing: Changing perspective on a feared event
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.impermanence: Understanding that forms change but essence remains

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dhira (The sober, self-realized person who is not bewildered by physical changes)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna explains the mechanism of reincarnation. The body is constantly changing, yet the conscious observer (the soul) remains constant. Death is simply the soul discarding one unworkable machine and receiving another. A self-realized person (dhira) understands this and is not deluded by death.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a profound cognitive reframing exercise. Krishna demystifies death by linking it to a common, non-threatening experience (aging). By observing that we have already 'survived' the death of our childhood body and our youth body while our consciousness remained intact, we can logically deduce that physical death is just another physical change, reducing the terror associated with it.
